algorithm.buffer_free: after a vector's element walk, if its begin pointer is non-null the routine calls the sized delete with (begin, capacity_end - begin); a null begin skips the buffer free; an empty but non-null vector still frees its buffer
algorithm.element_disposal: for each 0x20-byte element, if the +0x00 data pointer equals the element's own +0x10 address the element is skipped (short string); otherwise the sized delete is called with (data, *(element + 0x10) + 1)
algorithm.no_writes: the routine never writes to the holder; all begin/end/capacity fields are left dangling and it returns no value
algorithm.order: vector A (+0x50/+0x58/+0x60), then vector B (+0x38/+0x40/+0x48), then vector C (+0x08/+0x10/+0x18); each vector's elements are freed before its buffer; the C buffer free is a tail jump to the sized delete
algorithm.unread_field: no element's +0x08 field is ever read

consumers.caller_fde: 0x5d7d5a8..0x5d7d740, itself a landing-pad region of a larger function (opens with __cxa_begin_catch, no prologue)
consumers.site_0x5d7d619: passes a stack holder at rsp+0x60, on an exception-cleanup path after __cxa_end_catch and a sized delete
consumers.site_0x5d7d6a8: passes a stack holder at rsp+0xd0, on an exception-cleanup path after a sized delete; the region then resumes unwinding

element_layout.capacity_or_inline_buffer: +0x10: inline buffer address for a short string, capacity for a heap string

main: no calls except the sized-delete PLT stub; the C buffer free is a tail jump to it

routines.name: three-array string teardown
routines.outputs: none; frees heap element buffers and vector buffers in A, B, C order

unknowns: What the holder object is and what fills the three vectors; the packet pins only the byte-level teardown behavior.
What the per-element +0x08 field holds beyond the layout inference (string length in the libstdc++ layout); the routine never reads it.
The caller function's normal path; only its two exception-cleanup teardown sites are pinned.
The malformed-holder case (null begin with non-null end), which cannot come from a well-formed vector and is not pinned.
